title: Ten daily activities with the highest VBR resultant force (range of maxima per patient)
subcategory: VBR resultant force, high-load activities of daily living
condition: in vivo, VBR + posterior fixator, few days to 65 months post-op

quantity.name: maximum resultant force on VBR
quantity.definition: ABSOLUTE resultant force on the VBR; for each patient the range (highest and lowest) of the per-trial maximum resultant force over the n trials of that activity; load = carried/lifted weight belonging to the extreme values (chair = moving a chair).

source.authors: Rohlmann A, Pohl D, Bender A, Graichen F, Dymke J, Schmidt H, Bergmann G
source.n: 5 patients (4 M, 1 F) with telemeterised VBR (L1 in WP1-WP4, L3 in WP5); >13,500 trial datasets, 97 sessions
source.sample: in vivo, A3 compression fracture, posterior internal fixator + telemeterised VBR; measurements from a few days to 65 months post-op

WP1.note: VBR slightly eccentric (X-ray); thoracic kyphosis increased during follow-up

WP2.note: VBR implanted ~5 mm eccentric to the right

protocol.summary: Database of ~1000 activity/parameter combinations; top-10 activities by maximum resultant force pooled over 5 patients; walking given for comparison.
how_to_simulate: Model the patient (Table 1 anthropometry; L1 VBR for WP1-WP4, L3 for WP5)

Reproduce the activity (e.g. lifting a crate of the stated weight from the ground, forward elevation of straight arms holding the weight, moving the weight laterally in front of the body at hip level, sit-to-stand, stair walking, tying shoes, upper-body flexion)
Output the peak resultant force at the implant level during the activity

A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator; rank order of activities (lifting > arm elevation with weight > ... > walking) is a robust target

WP1.note: VBR slightly eccentric (X-ray); thoracic kyphosis increased during follow-up

WP2.note: VBR implanted ~5 mm eccentric to the right

subject_model.source: Rohlmann 2014a Table 1 (sex, age, height, body mass, fractured vertebra, fixator level, sessions, trials); VBR sagittal inclination from Discussion

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load. Database search: for each patient the 10 exercises with the highest absolute difference from the supine preload value were identified, then pooled over patients to the overall top-10. Values are the patient maxima over all trials and sessions (few days - 65 months post-op), exercises performed in the patient's own way; large intra/inter-individual variation. Italic (not in that patient's own top 10) and bold (peak over patients) formatting is noted per row where read. Text: highest resultant force 1650 N when lifting a 10.8 kg crate from the ground (WP4 printed 1649 N); other activities >1200 N: forward elevation of straight arms with up to 9.2 kg, moving up to 10.8 kg laterally in front of the body at hip level, sit-to-stand; walking ranked 11th; lowest forces always WP3.
